text: Event [Lat. eventus , from evenire , to happen]: Ger. Ereigniss ; Fr. évènement ; Ital. evento , avvenimento . Any change in the world of FACT (q.v.). The notion of event covers objective phenomenal changes and sequences of all sorts. The common usage makes the event a matter of time; and this is emphasized by the usage according to which events are the subject-matter of history, that is, each event is in relation to a series of happenings in time. Whether events may take place out of time would seem to depend upon one's general theory of time in relation to reality. ( J.M.B. )
